drills.q: Explain CALL vs DELEGATECALL vs STATICCALL: what changes, what persists?
drills.a: CALL: callee context - their storage, msg.sender becomes calling contract. DELEGATECALL: caller's storage + preserved msg.sender/value, foreign code only - the proxy primitive and the most dangerous opcode. STATICCALL (Byzantium): read-only frame, reverts on state writes.

drills.q: Where does uint128 a; uint64 b; uint64 c; uint256 d; land in storage? Gas implication of writing all four?
drills.a: a+b+c pack into slot 0 (16+8+8=32 bytes), d takes slot 1. Writing the packed trio = up to one SSTORE on slot 0 vs three separate 20k/2.9k writes unpacked. But reads pay per slot touched - keep hot fields with hot fields.

drills.q: Why does a naive proxy store its implementation pointer at keccak(...)-1 instead of slot 0 or 1?
drills.a: EIP-1967: pseudo-random slots like keccak256('eip1967.proxy.implementation')-1 (0x360894...) can never collide with realistically declared Solidity variables which occupy low sequential slots. Early structured-storage proxies collided exactly this way.

drills.q: Cost math: event vs storage for recording a transfer. When must you use storage anyway?
drills.a: Event: ~375 base + 375/topic + 8/byte ~ 1.3k gas typical Transfer; storage fresh write 20000, update 2900. Events are OFF-CHAIN only - no contract can read past receipts - so any value logic branches on must live in storage.

drills.q: Walk through msg.sender across user -> proxy -> implementation -> external token call.
drills.a: EOA->proxy: EOA. Proxy->impl via delegatecall: still EOA (context preserved). Impl->token via CALL: token sees proxy address, not EOA - hence approve/transferFrom dances and ERC-2771 meta-tx sender-forwarding patterns; tx.origin auth breaks here.

drills.q: Reconstruct the Parity multisig disaster precisely and name today's defenses.
drills.a: Shared wallet LIBRARY had public default-initializable functions: July 2017 attacker took ownership via init; Nov 2017 someone triggered its suicide(), freezing 513k ETH (~$150M then) in dependent wallets forever. Today: initializer modifiers, pre-initialized/disabled-initializer deployments, owned bases, no shared mutable libraries.

drills.q: UUPS vs transparent proxy - pick one for a new protocol and defend against UUPS's main failure.
drills.a: UUPS default: cheaper minimal proxy, atomic upgradeToAndCall. Main failure = bricking (bad impl consumes last chance) - mitigate with fork-tested upgrades, authorization guards on upgrade fns, deploying implementations pre-initialized, emergency pause. Transparent costs per-call gas but keeps upgrades in simpler proxy code.

drills.q: Design initialization for an upgradeable system with modules and roles.
drills.a: Single initialize() with initializer guard, reinitializer versions per module; deploy impls pre-initialized; wire admin/upgrader/pauser roles during init then transfer LAST to Safe+timelock to avoid front-run windows; verify post-init storage on a mainnet fork. Atomic init via upgradeToAndCall closes interim-state attacks.

drills.q: Diamond selector clash: how does it manifest and how do you catch it before mainnet?
drills.a: Two facets claim one selector; proxy routes silently to the winner - wrong auth/storage assumptions, fund-loss shapes; crafted collisions were exploited deliberately. Catch: CI asserting global selector uniqueness across facets, diamondCut rejecting duplicates, loupe introspection tests.

drills.q: Should this system be upgradeable at all? Give the decision procedure.
drills.a: Enumerate change classes expected (bugfix/parameter/logic); threat-model the admin path (key compromise = total loss?); check trust constraints (immutable sells neutrality); define exits (migration contracts, pausable bridges). Immutable if setters suffice; upgradeable only if iteration is certain AND governance credible (multisig + 1-7d timelock + monitoring). Immutables die with bugs; upgradables die with keys.
